notes: Introduction and abbreviations: no game mechanics.

Physical inventory (map, counters, cards, die): nothing to implement.

Hex scale is flavour; TEC movement costs come from data (the TEC values themselves are the data audit's).
Mountains are hexside features; a full Mountain hex behaves as Hill + six Mountain hexsides. Whether a hexside is "fully" mountain is a map-data call (data audit).
Classification by hex centre is decided when the map is encoded (one terrain per hex in data/salerno43/map.json); belongs to the map-data audit.
Heading only; its rules are the cases 2.3.1-2.3.5.
Every combat unit (BH, ASU, garrisons, free-stacking units) projects a ZOC; markers are state flags, not units.

MA = most MPs spent and still attack. fixed: a unit that used Extended Movement beyond its MA could still attack (now refused; the move records mpSpent). Elite/Low Quality read from data; note no counter is flagged lowQuality in data/salerno43/oob.json (check against the counters in the data audit).
Mech/non-mech, infantry and vehicle types per category; recon doubles in Hill/Marsh/City, silhouetted tanks do not.
British and Canadian units count as Commonwealth.
1/2/3 steps from the counter backs; a 3-step unit's third step is a Remnant (10.4).
Weather, German and Allied player turns (Initial, Movement, Combat, Recovery, Supply), Victory check. The contents of each step (weather, supply, replacements, rally, isolation) belong to 13-25.
Heading only; its rules are the cases 4.1-4.4.
Six stacking points; markers are not units.
0-value units stack free.
First silhouetted tank in a hex is free, others count 1.

Moves may not end overstacked; excess is eliminated at the end of the phasing player's Movement and Combat Phases. fixed: the limit was not checked at the moment an Auto DS is resolved (now enforced first, the declaration refused if the odds then fall below 10-1). The engine, not the player, picks which excess unit goes (cheapest step). The check at each Breakthrough attack is part of 15.x (other audit).
Heading only; its rules are the cases 5.1-5.8.
Units move one at a time, once per phase, never into enemy-occupied hexes. There is no stack-move action: a stack is moved unit by unit (same result; dropping off is moving fewer units).
Road rates, bridges where roads cross rivers, road rate into/out of EZOC. S2.3.4 (8th Army roads) is the S-rules audit's.
+3 MPs, never into an EZOC; may start in one if the first hex leaves it.
One or two hexes regardless of cost, stop on entering EZOC, no bonds, no prohibited hexsides; may attack.
+1 MP infantry; vehicles only as first hex of a Tactical Move (not in Rain) and become 1/2 Eff.
Infantry cross by Tactical first hex (1/2 Eff); vehicles only by road or pass; one mountain crossing per move.

Attack halved, advance max 1, no attack across mountain (vehicles: river), dropped if not ending adjacent to the enemy, removed in Recovery. fixed: a unit already 1/2 Eff could make a voluntary move earning a second marker the same turn. Naval Transport / airdrop sources of the marker are 18/21 (other audit).
Two German non-mech units, MA 5 as mechanized, attack 0, removed in Recovery. fixed: supply for trucks was taken from the last Supply Phase marker; it is now traced at the moment of the move.
Heading only; its rules are the cases 6.1-6.3.
Six adjacent land hexes, not across all-sea hexsides; vehicle ZOCs cross mountain hexsides only at roads/passes.
Stop on entering EZOC, +2 MP to leave, EZOC to EZOC allowed unless a bond is in the way.
Pointer rule; the effects themselves are tested under 12.2 (here), 14.4 and 16.3 (other audit).
Heading only; its rules are the cases 7.1-7.6.3.
Good Order, non-free-stacking units two hexes apart form Hex or Hexside Bonds.
No entering/crossing in movement, retreat across one eliminates, no advance across except into the vacated hex, no supply trace across.
Hexside Bond broken by enemies on both sides of the hexside, Hex Bond by an enemy in the intervening hex, at once.
Neither side crosses the other's bond.
Hexside Bond (never Hex Bond) with a friendly Entry Area only.
Heading only; its rules are the cases 7.6.1-7.6.3.

fixed: a bond across two non-road mountain hexsides was allowed when one of them had a road-less pass; now only roads lift the block. Hexside bonds may be pushed round a ridge but not into an enemy unit; vehicles need a road.
No bond with or across the coast.
Bonds form across minor river hexsides (the game has no major rivers).
Heading only; its rules are the cases 8.1-8.7.2.
Voluntary, once per unit and per hex each Combat Phase (breakthrough exception is 15.x), whole hex defends together, no attack across a hexside the unit could not cross.
One target hex per combat, from up to six hexes.

Odds rounded down (rulebook examples), shifts, variable strength revealed before the roll, losses, DD/retreat, advance. Defensive Air is committed by a standing order (options.defensiveAir) rather than asked each combat.
Heading only; its rules are the cases 8.4.1-8.4.6.
MAF full strength, the rest halved rounding up (8.4.3 example totals 20).
Divisions, Darby's Rangers and the Commando Brigade are formations.

One attachment stacked with a MAF unit (Allies: silhouetted tank or battalion; Germans: any). fixed: the attacker could not name the attachment (engine always auto-picked); attack actions now take attach and refuse an ineligible one.
Independent units (incl. 2/509 and BHs) belong to no formation but may attach.
20-point cap per side after doubling/halving (both rulebook examples).
Parenthesized strength only when alone, only one counts, losses last.
Heading only; its rules are the cases 8.5.1-8.5.2.
US and CW never attack together; may defend together and bond.
5th and 8th Army never attack together (8th Army units per S-rules data).
Heading only; its rules are the cases 8.6.1-8.6.2.
Below 1-3 refused; 8-1/9-1 on 7-1; 10-1+ automatic DS.

Virtual columns beyond 7-1 and below 1-3; limits applied to the net shift (rulebook examples). fixed: a 1-4 (or worse) lifted to 1-3 by shifts was refused outright; now allowed, and the minimum is judged before the defender's air shift.
Heading only; its rules are the cases 8.7.1-8.7.2.
Movement Phase only, MAF/coordination apply, Tank and Elite shifts only, DS at once, survivors 4 hexes Full Retreat, Auto DS units stop and skip regular combat (rulebook example incl. stack B's 4-1).
Advance after all combats at the full rate, markers removed. "Only one stack may Breakthrough" is 15.4 (other audit).
Heading only; its rules are the cases 9.1-9.9.
Halve per unit rounding up, never more than once; halved and doubled = printed.
Shift summary; US/CW air and naval support only their own nationality (defending: a unit of that nationality in the hex); max one Division + one Corps (Naval counts as Corps).
Heading only; its rules are the cases 9.3.1-9.3.4.
Tank in MAF and better best rating; ratings compared, not added (examples A/B/C).
Defender's shift when the attacker has no tank in the MAF or a lower best rating (examples A/B/C).
No tank shift vs Hill/Marsh/full Mountain/City; tanks across a river or mountain earn none but still deny the defender's.
Tank destroyers -1 rating attacking only (examples A/B); which battalions are TDs is data (TANK_DESTROYERS list).
One air unit per side per combat, any range, then used. German air restrictions (22.2.2) are the other audit's.
Heading only; its rules are the cases 9.5.1-9.5.3.
Ready Division ASU in range, its division attacking, then Fired.
Ready Corps ASU (or Naval) in range supports any attack of its nationality.
At most two artillery shifts, one Division and one Corps.
Within 2 hexes of the sea, not north of Campanella Point, once per turn each, never with a Corps ASU. Battleships (19.4) are the other audit's; the coastline/area is map data.
Elite in MAF and no elite defender; never for the defender.

River doubling only if every attacker is across (examples X/Y); vehicles across rivers halved; Hill/Marsh/City double all but silhouetted tanks, ASUs and variable units; mountain halves, tanks/recon only by road or pass.
Disrupted halved, Full Retreat 0, OOS attackers halved, Rain one shift left.
Heading only; its rules are the cases 10.1-10.4.3.

Every result (A1, EX incl. Limited Advance for a 1-step defender, Dis incl. already-Disrupted to Full Retreat 2, DR2, A1/DR2, DRX, A1/D1, D1, DR4, DS) with its retreat length, DD eligibility and mech/non-mech advance. The CRT cells themselves are data (data audit).
Heading only; its rules are the cases 10.2.1-10.2.2.

Who picks is modelled (owner on A1/D1/A1-D1, opponent on EX/DRX/DS), but the engine always makes the pick itself (owner: cheapest step, opponent: dearest); no action lets a human choose the unit. it.fails test kept.

Attacker losses from the MAF; parenthesized units, units with no strength (Full Retreat) and units that retreated in earlier (12.5) last or never; defender's loss first. fixed: units in Full Retreat (no defense strength) could be picked before units that defended.
Flip, eliminate, Remnant on a 3-step unit's second loss.

Remnant of the right kind (US, CW, GE-REM129, 82 Abn, 22/7A) takes the hex and status; unit goes to the display.
Mandatory elimination when no Remnant is left works; the owner cannot decline an available Remnant (loseStep always uses one). it.fails test kept.
Remnant eliminated: unit to Eliminated Box, Remnant back to the display for reuse.

Only with a surviving step and a result that allows it; success cancels retreat, disruption and advance.

CRT losses first; defender names the Lead Unit (auto-picked if not named); City / Clear-without-town / Other column. fixed: the defender could not name the Lead Unit (defend action now takes lead, validated).
Orange (data "y") gives -1; red ("r") allows no DD, Desperate included.
Good Order combat unit, not an ASU, not retreated in this phase; none = no DD; the Lead Unit takes the DD step losses.

+1 Elite, -1 Low Quality, -1 orange, +1 support, capped at +2 (+3 with Valiant/Warspite, 19.4, other audit). Low Quality is exercised by flagging a unit in the test since no counter is flagged in data.

One Ready Air/Naval/ASU, same nationality as the Lead Unit, division ASU needs a unit of its division in the hex, declared before the roll, then flipped. fixed (with 11.2.1): support of another nationality than the Lead Unit was accepted.

All seven results applied (-/1, -/-, P, D, -/1 H, 1*/1 H with the defender picking the attacker's loss, 1/dis H). Table values are data (data audit).
A lone one-step defender dying in a successful stand gives a Limited Advance.
Defender chooses Delay or -/1 H (defend.prefer).
Failure: full CRT retreat (Disrupted) and full advance, unless Desperate.

Roll on, a step per failure, until held or all eliminated.
Only if a retreat would eliminate a unit, or losing a port/BH hex would leave the stack OOS at the end of its retreat.

Rulebook example reproduced (from after the 5H/46 loss, since D1 losses are engine-picked, see 10.2.1). Support DRM applies to each roll. Gap: after each failed roll the engine keeps the named Lead Unit or picks the best one itself; the player cannot name a new Lead Unit between rolls.
Units that can retreat do; the rest fight a Desperate Defense.
Heading only; its rules are the cases 11.6.1-11.6.3.

Delay: 1-3 hexes by choice (defend.delay), Disrupted, Limited Advance; Desperate: first Delay = fail, second = -/1 H. fixed: a 1-hex Delay (and any retreat) took an extra hex beyond the required length whenever that scored better, though the extra hex is only allowed to avoid elimination (12.2).
P in a City places the City Battle marker and holds; further P there = Delay.
fixed: the marker stayed after the defender left the city, and "no enemy adjacent" was only checked in the Recovery Phase; both are now checked before every action.

Heading only; its rules are the cases 12.1.1-12.1.5.
Length from the CRT (2/3/4, Delay 1-3); reaching a friendly Entry Area fulfils it (offered as an option; the AI default prefers the full on-map retreat by score).
Retreats pass through friendly units without disturbing them. Gap: a stack always retreats together along one path (except the 11.5.4 split); the owner cannot split it. it.fails test kept.

Guidelines applied as priority filters: no elimination, every hex farther away, later hexes clear of EZOC (fixed: guideline 3 was not applied), in supply, no mountain crossings. Human owners may pick among equal-loss options (options.chooseRetreats).
May end overstacked; culled at the end of the owner's next Movement Phase (4.4).
May stop early in a friendly-controlled City, or (Allies) in a hex with a Beachhead unit; status still applies.

Eliminated: no hex but enemy ones, into/across a bond, two consecutive vacant EZOC hexes, ending in a vacant EZOC (one extra hex allowed only to escape it; fixed: the extra hex was also taken when not needed), off-map except a friendly Entry Area (no off-map hexes exist in the search), MA 0, prohibited hexes/hexsides. Friendly units that have not retreated negate EZOCs. Rulebook example 2 reproduced.

Vehicles die crossing an unbridged river; others unaffected.
Vehicles die crossing a non-road, non-pass mountain hexside; others 1/2 Eff; two such crossings eliminate anyone.
Full advance even if the retreat eliminated the defender.

Units that retreated in earlier this phase add no defense, cannot lead or take losses, and die if they must retreat again; not in Breakthrough Combat (breakthrough flag; that path is tested under 15.x by the other audit).
